case_study_insert.main_stem: Quarry Lane E-Commerce (QLE) is a cooperative based in Leeds in the online fashion marketplace sector, employing a workforce of 40. Led by Marcus Bell, the business connects independent designers with shoppers through its own website and operates a flat structure with democratic leadership. QLE plans to invest $320,000 in a cloud stock-control and packing hub, financed by a $200,000 bank loan and a $120,000 member share issue. It has fixed costs of $160,000 a year, a variable cost of $16.00 a unit and a selling price of $32.00, and currently produces 20,000 units a year. QLE faces two problems: packing errors have reached 2.6% and seller complaint cases are rising steadily.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Marketplace Operations Summary — Q3 2025: QLE handled 5,600 seller orders in the quarter, with a packing error rate of 2.6%, down from 4.0% a year earlier. Late deliveries fell from 51 to 28 per month. Average dispatch time is 4.6 days. A survey of 700 marketplace shoppers found 73% value fast, reliable delivery and 59% compare seller ratings before buying. A skills audit shows 11 of 40 staff have not been trained on the new cloud stock-control system; college training costs $780 per employee. Seller complaint cases rose by 18% last quarter.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Quarry Lane E-Commerce as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 3.25% to 3.90%, increasing borrowing costs for firms with variable-rate loans. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 7.1% from $13.10 to $14.03 per hour from April 2026, raising total wage bills. (3) Packing materials and cloud-storage input costs have risen 6.6% year-on-year, while online marketplace consumer spending grew 8.2%.

questions.question_text: QLE is funding part of its $320,000 expansion with a $120,000 member share issue. Explain two advantages for QLE of using a share issue rather than a larger bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Member shares bring in $120,000 with no interest or fixed repayment, so QLE can keep the $200,000 bank loan smaller and protect cash against fixed costs of $160,000 a year. That matters while packing errors run at 2.6% and late deliveries still reach 28 a month, because funds are not diverted to debt service when they are needed to improve service.

Point 2: Equity is permanent capital with no repossession risk, so the cloud stock-control and packing hub is secure even if the marketplace grows more slowly than expected. As a cooperative, a member share issue also spreads ownership among the people involved in the business, reinforcing the democratic structure and avoiding a lender's conditions that might restrict how Marcus Bell and the members run the platform.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to QLE's share issue, bank loan and expansion.

questions.question_text: QLE is promoting its marketplace to new shoppers. Consider online display advertising, sponsorship of a design fair, or social-media influencer marketing. Which should QLE choose to promote the platform? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Online display advertising: Banner and paid display ads can generate large volumes of impressions quickly and can be targeted by interest, driving traffic to the marketplace. However, display ads are often ignored and click-through rates are low, so much of the spend is wasted. For a cooperative funding a $320,000 hub with $160,000 fixed costs and a $200,000 bank loan, paying for impressions that do not convert into the 20,000 units handled each year is hard to defend.

Design fair sponsorship: Sponsoring a fair puts QLE in front of independent designers and fashion buyers, helping recruit sellers as well as shoppers and building credibility. It is a focused but geographically limited and short-lived channel; the costs of a stand and sponsorship can be high, and attendees may already be designers rather than the 73% of shoppers who value fast, reliable delivery that the platform needs to reach.

Social-media influencer marketing: The insert shows 73% of surveyed marketplace shoppers value fast, reliable delivery and 59% compare seller ratings before buying. Influencers can demonstrate reliable dispatch and explain seller ratings, link directly to the website and provide measurable engagement at modest cost. They reach a national audience beyond a single fair, though results depend on selecting credible, fashion-relevant partners.

Recommendation: QLE should choose social-media influencer marketing. It targets the exact delivery- and rating-conscious shoppers in the survey, is measurable and scales nationally. Online display advertising is rejected as wasteful and untargeted for a cooperative watching $160,000 fixed costs, and design fair sponsorship is rejected as narrow and short-lived for a platform that needs continuous traffic. QLE can keep a small fair presence to recruit designers, but influencers should lead the shopper campaign.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited description of the promotional options with minimal application to QLE.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of advantages and disadvantages of at least two options applied to QLE with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three options applied to QLE with a justified recommendation explaining why display ads and design fair sponsorship are rejected.

questions.question_text: QLE has a flat structure with democratic leadership and packing errors of 2.6%. Explain two benefits for QLE of this leadership style in the new packing hub.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership invites the 40 members to suggest improvements to packing routines, so practical ideas for cutting the 2.6% error rate and the 4.6-day dispatch time come from the people doing the work. A flat structure means these suggestions reach Marcus Bell quickly without passing through many management layers, speeding up problem-solving.

Point 2: Involvement raises ownership and motivation in a cooperative, which can help reduce the rising seller complaint cases and support the 59% of shoppers who compare seller ratings before buying. Engaged members are more likely to protect the 20,000-unit throughput needed to justify the $320,000 hub, and shared decisions reduce resistance to the new cloud stock-control system.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to QLE's error rate, complaints and structure.

questions.question_text: QLE must organise the new packing hub. Consider keeping a flat structure or introducing a hierarchical structure. Which should QLE choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Flat structure: A flat structure keeps decision-making close to the 40 members, supports the cooperative's democratic leadership and lets packing staff respond quickly to the 2.6% error rate and 28 late deliveries a month. It is cheap because fewer management layers are needed, and it suits a 20,000-unit operation. Its limits are a wide span of control for Marcus Bell and possible slow coordination as the $320,000 hub expands, with no clear promotion path for ambitious members.

Hierarchical structure: Extra layers would give tighter supervision, clearer roles and defined promotion routes, which might improve consistency in the packing hub and help train the 11 staff not yet trained on the cloud system. The disadvantages are slower communication, higher management cost against $160,000 fixed costs, and a clash with cooperative values that could reduce motivation and the member involvement currently helping to cut seller complaints.

Decision: QLE should keep a flat structure, adding only a small number of team coordinators rather than full layers. It preserves fast decisions and member motivation while the 2.6% error rate needs urgent attention and the $320,000 hub is new; a full hierarchy is rejected because its costs and communication delays would undermine the democratic culture and are unnecessary for 40 staff, and coordination can be improved with team leaders instead.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of flat and hierarchical structures with limited application to QLE.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of benefits and drawbacks of one or both structures applied to QLE.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both structures applied to QLE with a justified decision covering cost, communication and cooperative values.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how QLE's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $160,000 ÷ ($32.00 − $16.00) = $160,000 ÷ $16.00 = 10,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 10,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $32.00 − $16.00 = $16.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $16.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways QLE's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Comparing the 10,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 20,000 units shows a margin of safety of 10,000 units, indicating how far marketplace activity could fall before the $320,000 hub stops covering costs.
2. Contribution per unit of $16.00 lets managers model a lower fee or discount: a $2 reduction to $30.00 would leave $14.00 contribution, so they can judge whether more shoppers would still cover $160,000 fixed costs.
3. Fixed costs and contribution help check that the $200,000 bank loan can be serviced from contribution on 20,000 units before further borrowing is considered.
4. Unit cost data ($160,000 ÷ 20,000 units + $16.00 = $24.00 a unit) enables monthly benchmarking, so managers can monitor the 2.6% packing error rate and 4.6-day dispatch time as avoidable costs.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 10,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $16.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 10,000 units versus 20,000-unit output; modelling a $2 fee cut against $16.00 contribution; bank-loan servicing of $200,000; and unit-cost benchmarking at $24.00 to monitor 2.6% packing errors.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate QLE's liquidity position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has QLE's liquidity improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.50 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 2.00 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 0.70 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.20 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $72,000 inventories + $36,000 trade receivables + $27,000 cash = $135,000; 2025 current assets = $60,000 + $54,000 + $36,000 = $150,000. The 2024 liquidity comparison is $135,000 ÷ $90,000 = 1.50; for 2025 it is $150,000 ÷ $75,000 = 2.00. The stricter 2024 measure is ($135,000 − $72,000) ÷ $90,000 = $63,000 ÷ $90,000 = 0.70; for 2025 it is ($150,000 − $60,000) ÷ $75,000 = $90,000 ÷ $75,000 = 1.20.

Evaluation: Short-term solvency has strengthened clearly. The broader measure rose from 1.50 to 2.00 as current liabilities fell from $90,000 to $75,000 while current assets grew from $135,000 to $150,000. The stricter measure improved from 0.70 to 1.20, so QLE can cover short-term debts without relying on inventory — important while it services a $200,000 bank loan and builds a $320,000 packing hub. The more reliable signal is the stricter measure, because its improvement does not depend on stock that may not sell quickly for a marketplace of independent designers. However, trade receivables rose from $36,000 to $54,000, tying up cash, and seller complaint cases rose 18%, so faster settlement and tighter credit control are needed to preserve the gain.

Conclusion: QLE's liquidity has improved. Both the broader measure (1.50 to 2.00) and the stricter measure (0.70 to 1.20) show stronger short-term solvency without depending on inventory. The main residual risk is rising receivables, so Marcus Bell should tighten credit control before expanding the hub further.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of inventory, receivables and liability movements and a justified conclusion on whether liquidity improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for QLE of using cloud stock-control in its new packing hub.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Cloud stock-control gives real-time visibility of seller inventory, directly reducing the 2.6% packing error rate and the 4.6-day dispatch time by ensuring the correct item is packed and dispatched. That supports the 73% of shoppers who value fast, reliable delivery and the 59% who compare seller ratings, protecting the $32.00 selling price and the 20,000-unit throughput that underpins the $320,000 hub.

Disadvantage: The system adds to fixed costs and requires training — 11 of 40 staff have not been trained and college courses cost $780 each. If data is entered incorrectly or the platform goes down, orders could be delayed, worsening seller complaint cases that already rose 18% last quarter, and a flat structure may need new coordination roles to manage the change effectively.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to QLE's error rate, delivery data and costs.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base interest rate rise to 3.90%, the 7.1% minimum wage increase and the 6.6% rise in packing and cloud-storage input costs will affect QLE. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (3.25% to 3.90%): If QLE's $200,000 bank loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost increases by 0.65% of $200,000 = $1,300 a year (0.0065 × $200,000). Against $160,000 fixed costs this is modest, and the $120,000 member share issue carries no interest. Dearer credit could slow the 8.2% growth in online marketplace spending, but QLE can hedge by fixing the loan rate, so this remains a manageable pressure.

Minimum wage increase (7.1%, to $14.03 per hour): The insert gives 40 staff but no hours worked or pay rates, so a defensible annual wage bill cannot be invented. The proper test is productivity — 20,000 units ÷ 40 staff = 500 units per worker. If productivity holds, the rise is absorbable; if the 2.6% packing errors and 4.6-day dispatch time absorb staff time, unit labour cost rises and the $16.00 contribution per unit is squeezed. Training the 11 untrained staff at $780 each would help protect productivity.

Packing and cloud-storage cost inflation (6.6%): The insert does not decompose the $16.00 variable cost, so only a labelled bound can be calculated: if the whole variable cost rose 6.6%, that adds 6.6% × $16.00 = about $1.06 a unit; across 20,000 units this is roughly $21,120 a year (20,000 × $1.06). Even partial pass-through reduces contribution on every unit, and packing errors waste materials outright. QLE can offset part through the $120,000 equity cushion and by improving accuracy, but the effect is continuous.

Conclusion: The 6.6% rise in packing and cloud-storage input costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to all 20,000 units and directly erodes the $16.00 contribution that supports the $320,000 hub, whereas the interest rise is around $1,300 a year and hedgeable, and the wage effect can be offset if 500-unit productivity is maintained through training and better stock control.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to QLE.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on QLE's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes applied to QLE with a well-justified judgement that packing and cloud-storage input-cost inflation has the greatest impact and why the other two are smaller.
